facts.fact: Wavemaker exposes 13 MCP tools to Cursor, including generate_video, refine_video, scrape_and_analyze, plan_video, compose_video, render_video, generate_and_render, and get_cost_estimate.
facts.quote: Wavemaker exposes 13 of them, including `generate_video`, `refine_video`, `scrape_and_analyze`, `plan_video`, `compose_video`, `render_video`, `generate_and_render`, and `get_cost_estimate`.

facts.fact: MCP access is a Pro-tier feature; Free and Starter plans do not include it, per Wavemaker's own page.
facts.quote: MCP access is a Pro-tier feature. The Free and Starter plans don't include it.

facts.fact: Wavemaker's Pro plan costs $99 per month and unlocks API and MCP access along with priority generation and custom voice design.
facts.quote: Pro ($99/mo) unlocks API and MCP access along with priority generation and custom voice design.

facts.fact: Wavemaker's free web tier gives 75 credits, which the page says is enough for one video.
facts.quote: you can still create your first video free on the web (75 credits, enough for one video)

facts.fact: According to Wavemaker, a roughly 30-second video costs about 75 credits.
facts.quote: a roughly 30-second video runs about 75 credits, 60 seconds about 150, an image is 3, and a refine or edit is 15.

facts.fact: According to Wavemaker, generating an image costs 3 credits.
facts.quote: an image is 3, and a refine or edit is 15.

facts.fact: According to Wavemaker, a refine or edit costs 15 credits.
facts.quote: a refine or edit is 15.

facts.fact: Wavemaker prices video exports by resolution: 480p free, 720p 5 credits, 1080p 10 credits, 4K 25 credits.
facts.quote: Exports are priced by resolution (480p free, 720p 5 credits, 1080p 10, 4K 25).

facts.fact: Wavemaker's REST API is available on Pro and up and is built for programmatic generation at 30 requests per minute.
facts.quote: The API lives at `/api/v1/videos`, is available on Pro and up, and is built for programmatic generation at 30 requests per minute.

facts.fact: Wavemaker's remote MCP server authenticates with OAuth 2.1 using PKCE, so no API key is pasted into a config file.
facts.quote: The Wavemaker MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, which means you don't paste an API key into a config file.

facts.fact: Wavemaker's webhooks (HMAC-signed callbacks when a video is ready) are available only on the Business tier.
facts.quote: Webhooks are available on the Business tier.

facts.fact: The Wavemaker REST API rate limit is 30 requests per minute.
facts.quote: 30 requests per minute

facts.fact: Wavemaker's MCP and API access start on the Pro plan at $99 per month, which also includes 2,000 credits a month.
facts.quote: MCP and API access start on the Pro plan at $99/mo, which also includes 2,000 credits a month

facts.fact: Wavemaker's Pro plan includes 2,000 credits per month.
facts.quote: which also includes 2,000 credits a month

facts.fact: Wavemaker's Free and Starter tiers do not include MCP access.
facts.quote: The Free and Starter tiers don't include MCP.

facts.fact: Wavemaker lets new users create a video free on the web with 75 starter credits.
facts.quote: You can still create a video free on the web with 75 starter credits to try the product before upgrading.

facts.fact: Each Wavemaker refine_video edit costs about 15 credits.
facts.quote: Each refine costs about 15 credits and applies the change to your existing video.

facts.fact: Per Wavemaker's page, video generation takes a couple of minutes.
facts.quote: Video generation takes a couple of minutes.

facts.fact: According to the page, a finished Wavemaker video can run as a streaming TV commercial on 100+ networks through Adwave, starting from $50 (an Adwave service, separate from video generation).
facts.quote: can also run as a real streaming TV commercial on 100+ networks through Adwave, from $50

facts.fact: Wavemaker's MCP server is remote and hosted at https://wavemaker.adwave.com/mcp, so no local server is needed.
facts.quote: Wavemaker's MCP server is remote, hosted at `https://wavemaker.adwave.com/mcp`.

facts.fact: Wavemaker's MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and browser sign-in, while its REST API uses an API key.
facts.quote: Auth | OAuth 2.1 + PKCE (browser sign-in, auto-refresh) | API key
